chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, all from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had me read something from the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), and it contained: 'You are forbidden from the catfish, the glyptothorax, the sea horse, the floating fish, and the spleen.' I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you, fish without scales are brought to us.' He said, 'Eat what has scales from the fish, and do not eat what does not have scales.'

key_terms.الطَّافِي: Floating fish (often referring to dead or scaleless varieties)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for eating fish in Shia jurisprudence according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of the Four Scholars, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the general principle of fish consumption by linking permissibility to the presence of scales ('qishr'), resolving the ambiguity of species like catfish. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between halal and haram aquatic creatures, emphasizing the Prophet's family's authority in interpreting dietary laws beyond the explicit Quranic mentions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, altogether from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> made me read something from the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so there was in it – you have been forbidden from the catfish, and the glyptothorax (mountain catfish), and the sea horse, and the floating fish (dead), and the spleen. I said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! They come to us with fish with no scales on it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat from the fish what has scales for it, and what does not have scales for it, so do not eat it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr all from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, made me read something from the books of Aii, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Therein I found this: T prohibit you from using eel for food, al-Zimir, (a certain kind of fish), Mar mahi (something like fish), snake fish, dead fish floating on water and the spleen.’

I then asked, ‘O child of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah grant you kindness, ’People bring to us a kind of fish that has no scales.’ He (the Imam) said, ’You can use for food of fish that which has scales and do not use for food the kind of fish which has no scales.’”
